summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a complex medical history including quadriplegia, tracheostomy, GJ tube, atrial fibrillation, and type 2 diabetes was admitted from rehab for altered mental status and hypoxia. He presented with septic shock, severe hypernatremia, acute kidney injury, and diabetic ketoacidosis. Despite initial aggressive support with pressors, IV fluids, insulin, and broad-spectrum antibiotics, his condition remained critical. After extensive discussions with family, goals of care were transitioned to comfort measures only. He was managed with palliative medications and passed peacefully on hospital day 12. The family declined post-mortem evaluation.
